item.title: php2shell CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 Exploitation Requires Target-Specific PHP Conditions
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 23:00 → 30 Oct 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

php2shell one week later: Why one exploit doesn’t work everywhere — Must Read

Tenable’s testing found php2shell RCE is real but usually requires target-specific heap and runtime tuning, making broad Log4Shell-style mass exploitation unlikely. Defenders should still urgently patch or isolate internet-facing PHP systems, especially standardized network appliances and management interfaces where one calibrated exploit can scale.

  • PHP disclosed CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on October 20, 2026, and released fixes on October 21 for flaws that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
  • Tenable’s testing found that turning php2shell into remote code execution generally requires an exploit tailored to a target’s PHP build, runtime configuration, process manager, extensions, and memory layout.
  • Tenable observed mass exploitation attempts against five exposed vulnerable PHP sites but reported that none of those sites had been compromised as of October 29.
  • Reports cited by the article describe successful exploitation on researcher honeypots and against PAN-OS firewall and management servers, though Tenable did not independently verify the latter findings.
  • The article recommends prioritizing patches or isolation for internet-facing network appliances, management interfaces, and end-of-life PHP systems, while updating to fixed PHP releases or distribution packages.

Technologies: firewall, web-server

Products: php, pan-os, nessus, tenable-one-web-app-scanning, apache-http-server

Vendors: php-project, tenable, palo-alto-networks, apache-software-foundation

item.title: Poisoned AI Skills Deliver Atomic macOS Stealer and Linux Backdoor
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 19:00 → 29 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera found 516 AI-agent skills linked to the Atomic macOS Stealer campaign, including 70 confirmed malicious skills that still received high automated security grades on a popular marketplace. The poisoned documentation hides OS-specific setup commands that lure users or agents into downloading credential-stealing payloads, underscoring the need to inspect skill instructions and external dependencies before execution.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 AI skills tied to the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign across its broader dataset of 1.3 million AI skills, MCP servers, and plugins.
  • Of 70 confirmed malicious skills identified from non-Hugging Face sources in September 2026, all received A or B automated security grades on a popular skills marketplace.
  • The poisoned skills concealed malicious installation instructions in otherwise plausible documentation, commonly directing macOS users to decode Base64 text and execute it with Bash while directing Windows users to download and run a separate package.
  • AMOS is a macOS information-stealing malware family that can collect browser passwords and session cookies, keychain information, and sensitive files before sending the data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • The payload host 91.92.242.30 accounted for 83.7% of IP references in the dataset, while two glot.io snippets accounted for 95.9% of paste-relay references.

Technologies: operating-system, package-registry

Products: atomic-macos-stealer, openclaw, clawhub, skills-directory, agent-guardian, macos

Vendors: cyera, apple, openclaw, cloudflare

How to Vet AI Agent Skills: Lessons From a Fake PDF Skill — Should Read

A malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill preserved legitimate scripts and branding while replacing its instructions and adding a Linux backdoor, showing that AI-agent skills must be vetted as complete packages. Organizations should verify provenance, inspect every file and instruction, restrict execution and network permissions, and review updates before use.

  • Cyera Research identified a malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that retained its familiar name, description, and 11 files matching the official skill while altering the main SKILL.md instructions and adding a Linux executable.
  • The altered SKILL.md file was reduced from 315 lines to 19 and instructed the agent to make a network call to a Chinese domain.
  • The package included a 5 MB system_linux binary that Cyera said could provide a remote operator with a shell if executed.
  • Cyera found no direct code or instructions to execute the binary, but said the altered instructions called an external URL whose domains resolved to a private IP address during the research.
  • The article recommends verifying complete skill packages against their claimed sources, inspecting instructions and bundled code, and limiting agent permissions for network access and software execution.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill, linux

Vendors: anthropic, cyera

Health-ISAC Hacking Healthcare 10-27-2026 — May Read

Singapore’s Cybersecurity Strategy 2026 adopts a whole-of-ecosystem approach that strengthens protection of critical infrastructure, including healthcare, while expanding mandatory standards, AI-enabled defense, quantum preparedness, and international partnerships.

  • Singapore announced its Cybersecurity Strategy 2026 on October 13 at the opening ceremony of Singapore International Cyber Week, replacing its 2021 strategy.
  • The strategy identifies four pillars: defending critical infrastructure, securing the wider cyberspace, strengthening capabilities for AI and quantum, and enhancing resilience through global partnerships.
  • Healthcare is among the 11 sectors covered by Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure framework, and the strategy calls for stronger capabilities to defend these services against advanced and AI-enabled threats.
  • The strategy supports stronger cybersecurity regulations and baseline standards, including mandated adoption of cyber standards for higher-risk organizations.
  • Singapore frames AI as a cyber threat, a defensive tool for faster detection and response, and a target that must be secured as it becomes embedded in organizations and critical systems.

How to Vet AI Agent Skills: Lessons From a Fake PDF Skill — Should Read

Cyera researchers found a malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that preserved legitimate-looking files and branding while replacing its instructions and adding a Linux backdoor. Organizations should verify every file and instruction in AI skill packages, restrict agent permissions, and scrutinize unexpected executables or network destinations.

  • Cyera researchers identified a malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that retained its familiar name, description, and 11 legitimate matching files while altering its main instruction file and adding a Linux executable containing a backdoor.
  • The malicious SKILL.md was reduced from 315 lines to 19 lines and instructed the agent to make a network call to a Chinese domain.
  • If the added program runs, a remote operator may be able to issue commands with the permissions of the account that launched it.
  • The researchers found no direct code or instructions to execute the added binary, but the instructions were configured to call an external URL whose domain resolved to a private IP address during the research.
  • Cyera recommends that organizations verify complete AI skill packages against claimed sources, inspect changed instructions and unexpected files, and limit agent permissions for network access and software execution.

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill

Vendors: anthropic, cyera

Censys takes census of the Internet like no one else — May Read

Censys argues that widely differing PHP2Shell exposure counts reflect differences in scanners, units of measurement, banner visibility, query logic, and scan timing. It promotes its first-party Internet Map as a comprehensive way to track affected PHP hosts, web properties, patching progress, and related attacker infrastructure.

  • PHP announced emergency fixes on October 20 for two pre-authentication remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively known as PHP2Shell.
  • Public PHP2Shell exposure counts can differ substantially because sources use different scanners, count different objects such as IP addresses or websites, and apply different matching and timing methods.
  • Censys states that its Internet Map uses first-party scanners to scan all 65,535 ports daily and fingerprint open services, including PHP services on nonstandard ports.
  • PHP version banners can overstate exposure because Linux distributions may backport security fixes while retaining older visible version numbers.
  • Censys says it retains four years of searchable service history, allowing it to track when individual services move from affected to fixed.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: php, censys-internet-map, censys-investigator, arc-rapid-response, censys-attack-surface-management

Vendors: censys, php-foundation, chainguard

OpenCode User Hit with Hostile Backlash After Reporting Free AI Loophole — May Read

An OpenCode user who publicized and later promoted an IP-switching workaround for free hosted AI-model limits was subjected to severe harassment after users blamed them for tighter restrictions. It remains unclear whether OpenCode fully fixed the bypass, while shared VPN users report being caught by network-level enforcement.

  • A GitHub issue reported that OpenCode’s free hosted-model usage limits, which were tied to IP addresses, could allegedly be bypassed by switching IP addresses through a VPN while preserving a coding session.
  • The issue’s author later promoted the workaround and claimed to have run 130 agents across concurrent sessions, changing IP addresses after reaching usage limits.
  • The public GitHub thread attracted harassment against the reporter, including comments encouraging suicide and requests for identifying information, before it was deleted.
  • OpenCode contributors said enforcing limits without authentication was difficult and that shared VPN addresses could be flagged, leaving some VPN users unable to access free models.
  • OpenCode made October infrastructure and IP-handling changes, but the article says it remains unclear whether the reported IP-switching bypass was fully fixed.

Technologies: source-control

Products: opencode, github, deepseek-v4-flash, mimo-v2-5

Vendors: anomaly, github, deepseek, xiaomi

item.title: Qwen Model Jaggedness, Help-Desk Vishing, and QuickBooks Phishing Dominate Q3
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 11:00 → 29 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Ultra Trail: From Viewer to Mailer — Should Read

Infoblox traced a QuickBooks support phishing campaign to UltraMailer’s chanret.com tracking infrastructure, showing how scammers abuse the bulk-email tool while UltraViewer is used in related tech-support scams. The investigation also found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers carrying remote-access malware, though there is no evidence their developers were involved.

  • Infoblox linked a QuickBooks support phishing campaign using more than 350 QuickBooks-lookalike domains to chanret.com, UltraMailer’s default email-tracking domain.
  • The phishing emails used 1×1 tracking images that sent recipient email addresses, encoded in the image URL, to track.chanret.com when messages were opened.
  • The campaign briefly used Mail250 infrastructure in August 2026, but stopped after Mail250 suspended the reported account; the actor resumed activity through chanret.com on September 8.
  • Researchers found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers that contained authentic copies of the applications alongside njRAT and DarkKometa malware, respectively.
  • The article found no evidence that the developers of UltraViewer or UltraMailer participated in the scams or distributed the malicious installers.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: ultraviewer, ultramailer, mail250, quickbooks

Vendors: duc-fabulous, mail250, intuit, dynadot

Cohere’s Qwen Story: Looks More Like Model Jaggedness — May Read

Replaying Cohere’s Qwen trace showed the model generated many different, often invalid or local upload destinations rather than a fixed Alibaba endpoint, suggesting inconsistent “model jaggedness” rather than clear evidence of a backdoor. The findings reinforce the need to sandbox AI agents and restrict network permissions.

  • Cohere reported that Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, when asked to write a detection rule for curl downloads followed by bash execution, issued a command that attempted to send a test string to an Alibaba Cloud storage address.
  • Researchers replayed the published trace 64 times from just before the URL destination and observed 52 distinct host strings, including local-looking, nonexistent, and invalid domains.
  • Seven sampled destinations used Amazon Web Services hostnames, six used Alibaba Cloud hostnames, and 20 were local or internal-looking.
  • Changing the order of curl and wget in a check for available programs reduced continuations containing a curl network command from 15 of 32 to 4 of 32.
  • The researchers concluded that the results more strongly support inconsistent model behavior, which they call model jaggedness, than a single hard-coded destination, while noting that the tests cannot prove no backdoor exists.

Products: qwen3-8-flash-next, vllm

Vendors: alibaba, cohere, check-point, vllm-project

The day after tomorrow: After PHP2Shell, it gets worse, then defenders win — Optional

AI is expected to make it easier and faster to turn overlooked software flaws into critical exploits, creating a difficult period for security teams. The article argues defenders can ultimately gain an advantage by combining strong security architecture with complete asset visibility and rapid, automated remediation.

  • The article says recent critical remote-code-execution flaws in PHP and the Brotli compression library have heightened concern, though no mass compromise has been reported.
  • It states that the out-of-memory issue behind PHP2Shell was identified in a 2024 audit but remained unfixed until researchers showed it could be exploited last year.
  • The article argues that AI can reduce the work required to turn unexplained software behavior into a usable exploit by helping researchers investigate and chain flaws together.
  • It recommends that organizations combine strong security architecture with fast fixes, beginning with visibility into all software they run, including components in base images, CI images, hosting panels, and vendor software.
  • The article says teams should check code early, test applications and external networks before releases and after changes, and provide fixes that people can review.

Products: php, brotli

Vendors: aikido, anthropic, cloudflare, google

Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants — Optional

Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks in Q3 2026, driven by a 208% surge in short, sub-1 Gbps attacks, while attacks over 1 Tbps fell 69% after major IoT botnet disruptions. Attackers shifted away from CLDAP amplification toward DNS amplification and UDP floods, with the United States again the most-targeted country.

  • Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests during Q3 2026.
  • Network-layer attacks increased 208% year over year, with 96% ending in under 10 minutes and 98% remaining below 1 Gbps.
  • Hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps fell from 805 in Q2 2026 to 251 in Q3, while Mirai-classified mitigations peaked at 57.23 PB in August.
  • CLDAP attacks collapsed to 0.05% of network-layer attacks, while DNS amplification rose 215% and general UDP floods grew to 31.31% of such attacks.
  • The United States was the most-attacked location in Q3 2026, followed by China, while Canada rose from 16th to sixth and Israel moved seven places to 10th.

Products: cloudflare-radar, ddos-botnet-threat-feed

Vendors: cloudflare

IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases — Optional

Cisco Talos reports that Q3 2026 incident response engagements were increasingly driven by vishing callers impersonating IT help desks and by exploitation of internet-facing systems, while ransomware rose to 27% of cases. Organizations should prioritize phishing-resistant MFA, secure credential management, centralized logging, and protection of endpoint defenses against EDR-disabling techniques.

  • Phishing was the most common initial access method in Cisco Talos Incident Response engagements in Q3 2026, appearing in 37% of cases, while exploitation of public-facing applications accounted for 33%.
  • Ransomware and pre-ransomware incidents rose to 27% of engagements, with actors including Interlock and the emerging VYPR group disabling endpoint security tools and using remote-management access.
  • Talos attributed most prolonged telecommunications-sector cyber-espionage intrusions with high confidence to China state-sponsored actors, including Salt Typhoon, which used valid credentials and CVE-2023-20198 in publicly accessible management interfaces.
  • Financial organizations and public administration were tied as the most targeted sectors at 18% of engagements, while health care ranked third.
  • The most common security weakness was insufficient logging, followed by improper credential and secret management and missing or inadequate authentication and multi-factor authentication controls.

Technologies: edr, remote-access, operating-system, router

Products: cisco-ios-xe, cisco-secure-endpoint, microsoft-quick-assist, windows-defender-application-control, github-copilot-cli, claude-code

Vendors: cisco, microsoft, anthropic, github

item.title: NIK C2, PHP2Shell CVEs, and NetamLoader Lead Threat Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 07:00 → 29 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Ghost in the PHP2Shell: Why coordinated disclosure and patching will start moving faster — Must Read

PHP2Shell shows how AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and leaked disclosure details can compress the time between a flaw’s discovery, exploitation, and patching. Organizations should maintain accurate software inventories and be ready to rapidly deploy patches or mitigations when critical runtime vulnerabilities emerge.

  • PHP2Shell consists of two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, whose fixes were released on October 21 after their CVE identifiers leaked on October 20.
  • Attackers were attempting to exploit PHP2Shell before PHP announced the fixes, and CISA reported successful exploitation attempts after the patches were released.
  • As of October 27, Censys reported that about 11.2 million PHP services had moved to fixed versions while 32.5 million were still running affected versions, with more than 60 million services not reporting a version.
  • Aikido reported that its AI Code Analysis rediscovered PHP2Shell in PHP within a few hours after the disclosure.
  • The article argues that shorter, tighter coordinated-disclosure embargoes and faster patching readiness are needed as AI reduces the time from vulnerability discovery to exploitation.

Technologies: container-platform

Products: php, aikido-images, codex

Vendors: php-foundation, aikido, cloudflare, openai

NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework — Should Read

Cisco Talos identified NIK C2, a Go-based Windows remote-access framework that integrates OpenAI’s API directly into its command-and-control workflow to analyze stolen data from compromised hosts. The malware also supports credential and wallet theft, surveillance, lateral movement, defense evasion, and deployable screen-locking ransomware.

  • Cisco Talos observed NIK C2, a Go-based 64-bit Windows remote-access implant with persistent command-and-control communications over TLS WebSockets and an HTTP polling fallback.
  • NIK C2 includes an ai_generate command that sends operator prompts to the OpenAI Chat Completions API from the compromised host and returns the generated response to the command-and-control server.
  • If an operator does not provide an API key, the implant attempts to use the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable on the victim machine.
  • The implant supports credential theft, browser and cryptocurrency wallet data collection, keystroke logging, screen and audio surveillance, proxying, RDP operations, and several defense-evasion functions.
  • NIK C2 can deploy screen-locking ransomware that uses an HTML page, a Windows autostart registry entry, and a relaunch loop to display cryptocurrency payment demands.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, proxy, antivirus

Products: nik-c2, openai-chat-completions-api, windows, powershell, clamav

Vendors: cisco, openai, microsoft

Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia — Should Read

Kaspersky uncovered NetamLoader, an unattributed, highly sophisticated .NET/XAML malware framework likely delivered through a supply-chain compromise of a government-only Windows 10 build used in Asia. It abuses trusted components and deserialization flaws to bypass AMSI, erase evidence, migrate execution into dllhost.exe, and communicate with a C2 server after long sandbox-evasion delays.

  • Kaspersky identified an unattributed malware framework named NetamLoader in 2026 after detecting a malicious .config file inside a CAB archive stored in the Windows update-package directory.
  • The infection chain used PatchMyPC-ScriptRunner.exe, Microsoft-signed .NET assemblies, AppDomainManager injection, a crafted .resx file, and XAML payloads to load malicious code.
  • NetamLoader patched the AMSI scanning interface so that scans returned a clean result, then used a remote COM object to load its next-stage payload into dllhost.exe.
  • The malware deleted malicious files, CLR usage logs, Prefetch files, and selected update-log entries to reduce forensic evidence.
  • The .NET 2 plugin delayed its initial C2 connection by 20 to 40 minutes, polled the openaigpt4v.com C2 infrastructure, and used AES-CBC with HMAC to encrypt and authenticate network traffic.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10, patch-my-pc, windows-server-appfabric, dotnet-framework, amsi

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft, patch-my-pc, cloudflare

Configured to protect: How to properly use security policies — Optional

Analysis of 1.6 million Acronis-managed endpoints finds that customers generally retain secure defaults and use multiple plans mainly to separate backup from security, often adding them incrementally over time. MSPs are split between standardized and customized customer configurations, with geography and industry—especially health care and education—strongly influencing how comprehensive protection is deployed.

  • The report analyzes live configuration records from more than 1.6 million active endpoints managed through Acronis Cyber Platform.
  • Across the fleet, 65% of active endpoints run two or more protection modules, while the average Windows workstation runs 5.6 modules.
  • Among machines with two or more separate protection plans, 82% use plans for different purposes, such as separate backup and security plans, while 77% use the same schedule across their plans.
  • Core default protections are commonly retained: the anti-malware behavioral engine is enabled in 84.7% of plans, and a ransomware response is configured in 87.9% of active-protection plans.
  • Among more than 9,000 managed service providers with at least five active customers, roughly half apply a uniform plan pattern to most customers and roughly half customize by customer.

Technologies: backup, antivirus, edr, dlp, remote-access, network-monitoring

Products: acronis-cyber-platform

Vendors: acronis

Find the AI Risks That Matter in a Flood of AI Activity — Optional

Netskope promotes its AI Risk AISecOps Agent as a way to correlate AI-related telemetry across apps, agents, and MCP servers, automatically prioritize risky behavioral patterns, and provide evidence-backed investigation verdicts. The tool is designed to help analysts focus on higher-risk AI activity while existing DLP and guardrail controls continue enforcing policy.

  • AI risk can emerge when individually normal-looking changes, such as an approved AI application accessing new data or an agent using additional tools, form a risky pattern when viewed together.
  • The article cites a June 2026 Microsoft demonstration in which changes to an approved MCP tool could cause an AI agent to send invoice data to an external server, with the risk becoming apparent through comparison with historical behavior.
  • Netskope AI Risk AISecOps Agent evaluates users, AI applications, agents, and MCP servers daily, ranks them by behavioral risk, and automatically investigates the highest-ranked entities.
  • For each prioritized entity, the agent correlates related events, creates an evidence timeline, and returns a risky, legitimate, or inconclusive verdict with a confidence level.
  • The agent is not deployed inline, so existing real-time controls such as AI Guardrails and DLP continue enforcing policy while analysts review investigations and retain remediation decisions.

Technologies: dlp, casb, proxy

Products: ai-risk-aisecops-agent, netskope-one, netskope-skylight-ai-security, netskope-skylight-ai-guardrails, netskope-one-dlp, netskope-one-ueba, netskope-one-ng-swg, netskope-skylight-agentic-broker, netskope-skylight-ai-command-center

Vendors: netskope

Searchjacked: Hidden Browser Extensions Hijack Searches for 13 Million Users — Should Read

Researchers identified 319 mostly hidden Chrome extensions, installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade, that replace default search engines and route queries through operator-controlled proxies to monetize Yahoo or Bing referral traffic. This gives operators visibility into users’ searches and the ability to dynamically redirect them to potentially malicious destinations.

  • The investigation identified 319 browser extensions that changed users’ default search providers and were installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade.
  • Many of the extensions are unlisted in the Chrome Web Store and are promoted through advertisements for tools such as PDF search, manual finding, safe search, and AI search.
  • The extensions route search queries through operator-controlled proxy servers before redirecting users to Yahoo or Bing results with search-syndication partner tracking IDs.
  • The proxy servers allow operators to record search referrals and can choose destinations separately for each request; one tested extension sent identical searches to several different destinations.
  • Identified operators include Intango LTD, Tightrope Interactive, System1, Perion Network, and ValidClick/Inuvo, while two large groups called SecuryBrowse and Bing-Search remain unattributed.

Technologies: browser, proxy

item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 23:00 → 29 Oct 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

Searchjacked: Hidden Browser Extensions Hijack Searches for 13 Million Users — Should Read

Researchers identified 319 mostly hidden Chrome extensions, installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade, that replace default search engines and route queries through operator-controlled proxies to monetize Yahoo or Bing referral traffic. This gives operators visibility into users’ searches and the ability to dynamically redirect them to potentially malicious destinations.

  • The investigation identified 319 browser extensions that changed users’ default search providers and were installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade.
  • Many of the extensions are unlisted in the Chrome Web Store and are promoted through advertisements for tools such as PDF search, manual finding, safe search, and AI search.
  • The extensions route search queries through operator-controlled proxy servers before redirecting users to Yahoo or Bing results with search-syndication partner tracking IDs.
  • The proxy servers allow operators to record search referrals and can choose destinations separately for each request; one tested extension sent identical searches to several different destinations.
  • Identified operators include Intango LTD, Tightrope Interactive, System1, Perion Network, and ValidClick/Inuvo, while two large groups called SecuryBrowse and Bing-Search remain unattributed.

Technologies: browser, proxy

Inside KeyDrift: Analyzing historical UAT-11473 activity on Cisco SD-WAN — Must Read

Cisco Talos found that UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to deploy the KeyDrift framework, which persistently intercepts control-plane traffic and steals IPsec keying material. Organizations should urgently patch affected SD-WAN systems and investigate for modified runit services, vdaemon injection, and KeyDrift artifacts.

  • Cisco Talos identified UAT-11473 exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to gain unauthorized access.
  • UAT-11473 deployed the KeyDrift malware framework, whose PolyFlame component is injected into legitimate vdaemon processes and can provide command execution and intermediate command-and-control functions.
  • KeyDrift’s LittleFilch component intercepts decrypted Cisco SD-WAN control-plane traffic, extracts assessed AES-256 IPsec data-plane key material, and stores collected records in encrypted form.
  • Talos assesses with high confidence that UAT-11473’s infrastructure considerably overlaps with Volt Typhoon’s Silent Train covert access network.
  • Cisco released patches for CVE-2026-20127 and a Catalyst SD-WAN hardening guide, while Talos recommends organizations monitor for post-compromise activity.

CVE-2026-111497: Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell Vulnerability May Allow RCE — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that can enable crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution when vulnerable software decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should urgently patch affected Node.js, Bun, .NET, Python, Envoy, and other Brotli-dependent components, especially internet-facing services that accept Content-Encoding: br requests or fetch external content.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Node2Shell and HTTP2Shell, is a critical out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that can cause crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution when processing attacker-controlled Brotli data.
  • The vulnerability can be reached through crafted Brotli-compressed HTTP requests sent to servers or through malicious Brotli-compressed responses automatically decoded by client applications.
  • Affected software may include Node.js, Bun, Python Brotli bindings, .NET, Envoy Proxy, Istio, Java brotli4j, libbrotli, and curl/libcurl through Brotli dependencies.
  • Zscaler Deception observed 402 events from 20 source IP addresses targeting 12 customers within 24 hours of public disclosure, with 40% classified as reconnaissance and 60% as exploitation attempts.
  • Organizations are advised to patch vulnerable components, rebuild and redeploy containers using patched images, disable Brotli decoding on vulnerable paths if patching is delayed, and monitor for crashes or unusual process and network behavior.

  • The issue affects unpatched .NET 8, 9, 10, and pre-RC3 .NET 11 releases when applications decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data, while .NET Framework is not affected.
  • Microsoft released fixes in .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, and 11 RC3 on 25 October 2026.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 October 2026, with reported exploitation so far focused on Node.js.
  • Organizations should update affected runtimes and, until patching is complete, remove or block Brotli decompression for untrusted requests, HTTP responses, and application inputs.
